summary: Careful, well‑executed preregistered benchmark study that honestly reports a ceiling outcome and supplies comprehensive archival artifacts. The work fills a reproducibility gap by providing a sealed task generator, deterministic validator, and execution/analysis bundle; however, manuscript needs concise clarifications (task difficulty summary and the single failure case), explicit generation/determinism details, and clearer description of the shared‑initial design and repair trigger so readers can judge construct validity and reproducibility without inspecting external artifacts.
critical_issues: Insufficient in‑manuscript reporting of task difficulty distribution and the single baseline failure case; current text refers to archival artifacts but does not present minimal summary evidence needed to interpret the ceiling effect.

Unclear description of model generation determinism and sampling settings (temperature, sampling/deterministic mode, seeding) that are necessary to reproduce identical shared initial generations across baseline and guarded conditions.

Shared‑initial paired design and repair trigger policy materially constrained GVR engagement (repair stage executed once). The manuscript needs a clearer, explicit justification and discussion of how this design choice affects the confirmatory hypothesis and inference.

Repair invocation details are not described in the paper: the one repair call’s prompt/trace and the repair trigger logic should be summarized in‑paper (even if full traces remain in the archive) so readers can evaluate the repair policy’s practical behavior.
required_revisions: Add a concise in‑manuscript summary (single paragraph or a small table/figure) showing task difficulty distribution (counts by difficulty level) across the N=300 tasks and include the identifier and validator diagnostic for the single baseline‑failed task (task id, score_reason_code, validator violation fields). These values must be taken from the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json and quoted exactly.

Explicitly state model generation settings in the Methods (temperature, max tokens, top_k/top_p or policy used, and whether generation was deterministic), and cite the execution/model_configuration.json entry. Explain how identical shared initial outputs were enforced/expected between baseline and guarded (e.g., caching, single shared call, seeds, or provider determinism).

Expand the Methods paragraph that motivates and justifies the shared‑initial paired design and the preregistered repair budget/trigger policy. Explain (briefly) how this design isolates repair effectiveness and how it also limits GVR engagement when baseline already passes the validator.

Summarize the repair trigger logic and the content/location of any repair prompt(s) used. For the single repair call that occurred, report (in the paper) the repair provider trace path/sha256 (already archived) and a brief description of the repair action and why it was triggered. If the repair prompt is sensitive, include a short non‑sensitive synopsis and point to the archived trace for full details.
optional_revisions: Include the paired 2×2 contingency table and the exact McNemar test result as a small inline table (if not already present) to make the primary inference immediately visible without opening artifacts.

Add one representative example (short) of an intentionally harder synthetic task from the manifest as an appendix paragraph (within page limit) to illustrate the task encoding format and validator constraints.

Replace or supplement OpenAlex/identifier citations in the Related Work with conventional author–year venue citations where possible (for reader convenience), while retaining the verified reference list in the archive.
Briefly discuss in Conclusion concrete next steps (e.g., increasing repair budget or using stateful/emulated validators) and point readers to exact artifact paths needed to run such follow‑ups.
